A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Augmentation study. All 35 pages of v4 and 37 pages of v5, including Appendices A–E, are readable. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original Deep Augmentation experiments on sentence embeddings, vision and graph classification in Tables 1–3, with extensive ablations and representation analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports graph dropout-rate sensitivity results in Appendix C.1 and Figure 53.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated auxiliary PCA rule from subtracting the p-th principal component to projecting away the top p components. Dropout, stop-gradient and half-batch sampling remain unchanged. Retained single-component experiment descriptions leave the implemented PCA procedure unresolved.

E1.justification: Both retain Wikipedia/STS sentence experiments, CIFAR10/CIFAR100/ImageNet100 vision experiments, CIFAR transfer tasks, and COLLAB, IMDB-Multi, NCI1 and PROTEINS graph classification. The new graph ablation varies settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in corresponding experiments, including SimCSE, SimCLR, GCL and the MLM/supervised reference models. The new graph ablation compares Deep Augmentation configurations without adding a comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 adds an explicit graph evaluation sweep over dropout rates 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5, layers 0, 2, 4 and 6, and stop-gradient use, reporting test-set performance. Existing protocols remain stable; micro-F1 was already identified as f1mi in v4's graph plots.

E4.justification: New Figure 53 tests graph performance sensitivity to dropout rate and its interaction with layer depth and stop-gradient across four retained datasets. Existing vision/NLP ablations, transfer experiments, and alignment/uniformity and CKA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The standard deviations added to Table 3 duplicate those already reported for the corresponding rows in v4's Table 6. Existing uncertainty practices remain unchanged, with no new run-count, seed or statistical-testing information.

E6.justification: v5 adds graph test-result curves in Figure 53. Table 3 also corrects GCL+DeepAug's IMDB-Multi mean from 52.88 to 52.89, matching Table 6 in both versions without changing the ranking. Other matched results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the PCA definition with explicit centering, SVD and top-p projection, a mathematically different operation. Its new description inconsistently assigns d-dimensional right singular vectors to a d-by-K matrix. The added standard micro-F1 formula merely explains an existing metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and discussion retain the same central claims about deeper-layer augmentation, stop-gradient, PCA as an alternative, contrasting supervised behavior, and mitigation of inter-layer co-adaptation.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly qualifies the negative supervised results by explaining that the experiments use larger dropout rates, single-layer masking and other departures from conventional dropout. It emphasizes effect direction over absolute scores, adding a substantive qualification to the retained findings.

D1.justification: Figure 4 now specifies that it displays the best-performing dropout settings across the listed rates. Appendix C explains micro-F1 computation and clarifies validation-based selection for Table 6. These refine documentation of retained experiments; code links and established training details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The added publication and review notices do not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v5 adds acknowledgements, publication/review notices, Appendix C.1 and localized explanatory prose. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v5 adds the four-panel Figure 53, displays existing standard deviations in Table 3 and clarifies several captions. Retained appendix Figures 53–59 become Figures 54–60, with figures and tables reflowed; existing graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The graph sensitivity analysis, clearer reporting and supervised-dropout qualification provide limited benefits. However, v5's revised PCA definition introduces top-p projection while retained experiments still describe single-component removal, alongside an SVD dimensional inconsistency. Because the PCA alternative supports a core contribution, these gains and the new methodological inconsistency do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
